subject: MediSentry: scope for data erase / log retention exception
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medsentry.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medsentry.com
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: 180d request for debug/session traces and evidence needed

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our SOC 2 readiness checklist and a customer-specific regulatory carveout, our compliance team is asking whether Redwood can support a 180-day retention window for full request traces and debug-level session logs for our tenant (MediSentry).

Two points we need clarified:
1) Can you retain full request/response traces for 180 days for a single customer?
2) If yes, how do you handle PII in those logs (do you provide pseudonymization or scoped redaction)?
3) We also need artifact evidence for audit: a retention matrix, sample proof-of-delete workflow, and a CAIQ/SIG mapping showing where the change appears.

We understand default product TTL is shorter; this is a customer-specific exception tied to a regulatory pilot. Please let us know the technical approach, controls, and what evidence you can provide (PDFs/CSV/short runbook).

Best,
Elena Torres
Director, Compliance — MediSentry
[Attachment: internal-compliance-checklist.docx]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medsentry.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: 180d request for debug/session traces and evidence needed

Hi Elena —

Short answer: yes — we can support a tenant-specific extended retention for traces, but it requires a controlled exception and a combination of technical and contractual controls. Below is a short summary and proposed next steps.

Summary of options we can offer:
- Scoped retention: raw request traces can be retained for up to 180 days for a single tenant *if* PII fields are pseudonymized at ingest (hashing + salt managed by the customer) or redacted via a customer-provided mapping.
- Escrow for raw PII: if MediSentry requires unredacted raw traces, we can place raw artifacts in an encrypted escrow bucket retained for 180 days with strict access controls (SSE-KMS) and audit logging; normal runtime copies would be pruned sooner.
- Aggregation + sampling: to reduce risk, we can keep full traces for 30 days and sampled traces (1 in N) for 180 days for debugging and forensics; full forensic capture could be enabled temporarily during incidents.

Controls and evidence we can provide:
- Retention matrix (attached: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx) mapping default TTLs vs exception TTLs.
- Proof-of-delete runbook (we can produce a proof-of-delete CSV for sample keys and a signed attestation).
- CAIQ/SIG mapping excerpt showing where changes are reflected (we will add a "tenant-scoped retention" entry and provide the doc ring-fenced for your audit).

Operational impacts / notes:
- Escrow approach requires a contract addendum and a security review; escrow artifacts are charged as additional storage in Dedicated/Private plans.
- We will need a written Data Processing Addendum (DPA) amendment and a signed mutual action plan.
- Implementation lead time: ~2–3 weeks for SRE + product config, less if using pseudonymization at ingest.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm preferred approach (pseudonymize at ingress OR escrow raw artifacts).
2) I will loop in security and legal and deliver a draft retention addendum + evidence pack.
3) Schedule a short working session to align on fields that count as PII and test proof-of-delete flow.

Attaching initial retention matrix and a short escrow proposal PDF to accelerate. Happy to jump on a call this week.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx] [Attachment: medsentry_scoped-escrow-proposal.pdf]

Questions for you:

Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: 180d request for debug/session traces and evidence needed

Mateo / team —

Thanks for the clear framing. From security/compliance side we can approve a tenant-scoped 180-day retention for traces subject to the following hard constraints:

1) No raw PII in retained runtime traces unless stored in an encrypted escrow container with documented access procedures and quarterly access reviews. Escrow must use customer-managed KMS where feasible.
2) Pseudonymization at ingest (customer-provided salt or HMAC) preferred — document the mapping as part of the evidence pack.
3) We need a signed retention addendum in the DPA and a one-page attestation that outlines deletion proof steps (we'll produce a template).

If MediSentry agrees to the pseudonymization route, product can enable tenant TTL = 180d with minimal SRE changes; if they require raw PII escrow we will need legal + procurement signoff and an implementation window of ~3 weeks.

Deliverables we will provide once approach confirmed:
- Updated retention_matrix_v1 (final) as XLSX and CSV
- Proof-of-delete runbook & sample CSV of deleted keys (signed)
- CAIQ/SIG excerpt and an internal mapping doc showing SOC 2 control IDs affected
- A short runbook for auditors describing the escrow access review cadence

Elena — please confirm whether MediSentry will accept pseudonymization or needs escrow for raw artifacts. Once you confirm I will route the retention addendum to Legal and drop the evidence pack into the Drive link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Xq-example-retention-matrix
HubSpot record: HS-123456789

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
